claims.text: A machine-learning predictive approach trained on experimental data and defect-inclusive simulations will improve thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy for bulk HfNbTaTiZr in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
The proposed accuracy improvement will be particularly applicable to HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Including defect-inclusive simulations and experimental data allows the model to account for defect scattering.
Including defect-inclusive simulations and experimental data allows the model to account for anharmonic phonon interactions.
Existing analytical models do not capture defect scattering well.
Existing analytical models do not capture anharmonic phonon interactions well.
Existing analytical thermal-conductivity models used as the baseline assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
Accounting for defects, anharmonicity, and oxygen impurities will better capture the real-world thermal-conductivity behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
The machine-learning approach will reduce thermal-conductivity prediction error by at least 20% relative to existing analytical models across both stated temperature regimes.
The approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing up to 1 wt.% oxygen.
The approach is applicable within 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The magnitude of the accuracy improvement depends on the quality and quantity of the training data.
The magnitude of the accuracy improvement depends on the machine-learning algorithm used.
